name: The Ex
label: Touch and Go
lede: Four Amsterdam squatters drew straws for their instruments in 1979; the band they started has since played more than 2,000 shows in 45 countries, from CBGB to Ethiopian marketplaces, and never settled on one sound.

hero.by: The Ex in Germany, September 2016. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Two seconds with a spray can
eras.text: The Ex came out of the squats of Amsterdam and Wormer, inspired by The Fall and The Mekons, with lyrics about squatting, politics and the factory down the road. Nobody in the band had been to music school.

years.src: The Ex: History · The Quietus · Wikipedia: The Ex
years.h: Four squat kids draw straws to decide who plays what
years.p: [[Terrie Hessels|c9640d66-a766-46a4-a6a9-c6891864c348]], Jos Kley (soon G.W. Sok), Geurt and René pick "the Ex" because it was the shortest name on the list.
years.xp: "It was chosen because it was an easy one to spray quickly on a wall," Hessels told the Quietus. The band's own history says two seconds flat, and the first six months went mostly on a hit-and-run graffiti campaign.

years.src: The Ex: History
years.h: First gig at De Bakkerij in Castricum
years.p: After half a year of advertising on walls, the band plays its first show, in Castricum, north of Amsterdam.

years.src: The Ex: History · Wikipedia: The Ex
years.h: Disturbing Domestic Peace, with a free 7-inch inside
years.p: The first LP follows June's All Corpses Smell the Same EP. Soon after, both Geurt and René leave and the rhythm section starts turning over.

years.src: The Ex: History · The Quietus
years.h: The band squats a villa in Wormer
years.p: The same year the band puts out a benefit single, Weapons for El Salvador.
years.xp: The Ex's house in Wormer became a place to live, rehearse and put on shows in the living room and garden. "Sonic Youth stayed there in the early days and also the band Konono," Katherina Bornefeld told the Quietus.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Ex · The Ex: History
years.h: Jon Langford of the Mekons produces Tumult
years.p: In the autumn the band tours England for the first time, with Alerta. [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]] has them in for sessions in 1983, 1985 and 1986.

years.src: The Ex: History · Wikipedia: The Ex · The Guardian
years.h: Four 7-inches about one dead paper factory
years.p: Dignity of Labour is a box of singles and a book about the closed Van Gelder paper mill in Wormer, recorded partly in its ruins.

eras.title: Oil drums, miners and a red fire engine
eras.text: The lineup kept changing, and so did the instruments. Katherina Bornefeld arrived on drums, the band toured for striking British miners and behind the Iron Curtain, and by 1989 Sonic Youth were guesting on their records.

q: we never had an education at music school
years.src: Wikipedia: The Ex · The Ex: History · The Guardian
years.h: Katherina Bornefeld takes over the drums, and is still there
years.p: She joins the year of Blueprints for a Blackout, a double album with violin, oboe, marimba and oil drums, and a benefit tour for the striking British miners.

years.src: The Ex: History · Wikipedia: The Ex
years.h: Spanish Civil War songs, with a 144-page photo book
years.p: A double single of songs from the Spanish Revolution, packaged with archive photos from the anarchist union CNT. It sells best in England.

years.src: The Ex: History · Wikipedia: The Ex
years.h: A fluorescent red fire engine carries them across Eastern Europe
years.p: Poland, Czechoslovakia and Hungary, years before the Wall came down. With [[Chumbawamba|7b7b1e6f-e73e-41a0-9d72-8f0b30c6992d]], as Antidote, they cut the single Destroy Fascism!

years.src: The Ex: History · Wikipedia: The Ex
years.h: The band starts Ex Records and puts out its Peel sessions
years.p: Hands Up! You're Free collects the BBC sessions; Langford produces Aural Guerrilla, and "Rara Rap" goes after apartheid.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Ex · The Ex: History
years.h: First American tour, with two nights at CBGB
years.p: The band crosses with [[NoMeansNo|37e9d7b2-7779-41b2-b2eb-3685351caad3]]; Dutch broadcaster IKON films the CBGB shows for TV.

years.src: Wikipedia: Joggers and Smoggers · Wikipedia: The Ex
years.h: Thurston Moore and Lee Ranaldo turn up on Joggers and Smoggers
years.p: A double album cut in June at the squatted ADM shipyard, with Dog Faced Hermans, Instant Composers Pool players and a grill, birdcage, fire extinguisher and electric razor.
years.xp: Kim Gordon is on it too, by tape and telephone. AllMusic calls it the band's "magnum opus" and a turning point. Dog Faced Hermans' drummer Wilf Plum helped on the recording after the two bands toured together that year.

eras.title: A cellist and a singles club
eras.text: An American avant-garde cellist made them a jazz-festival band without taking away the guitars. Andy Moor came over from Dog Faced Hermans, and the band ran its releases like a club.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Ex · The Ex: History · The Guardian
yt: Live at the Vrije Vloer, Utrecht, 1990
years.h: Andy Moor of Dog Faced Hermans starts playing with the band
years.p: The London-born guitarist goes full-time in 1994, when the Hermans play their last show.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Ex · The Guardian
years.h: Subscribers pay 36 guilders, and the last single won't fit the box
years.p: For a year, a new 7-inch every two months. The final one was a 12-inch, too big for the box that came with the first.

years.src: The Ex: History · Wikipedia: The Ex · The Guardian
years.h: Tom Cora's cello on Scrabbling at the Lock
years.p: Made with the American cellist Tom Cora, it becomes the band's best-selling record, with an underground hit in "State of Shock". In January 1992 it wins them the Dutch BV Popprijs.
years.xp: The Guardian later called the Cora partnership the band's real move forward, the one that brought the jazz world to them. A second Ex-Cora album, And the Weathermen Shrug Their Shoulders, followed in 1993, with jazz-festival tours in Austria and Germany.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mudbird Shivers · The Ex: History
years.h: Han Buhrs brings a second voice on Mudbird Shivers
years.p: Out alongside Instant, a double CD of improvisations with Han Bennink, Ab Baars and Wolter Wierbos. After a party at the Paradiso, the band announces a year off.

eras.title: Albini, Touch and Go, Addis Ababa
eras.text: Steve Albini had been a fan for years; from 1998 he recorded them and Touch and Go put them out in America. In the same stretch the band started going to Ethiopia, and came back changed.

years.src: Wikipedia: Starters Alternators · The Ex: History
years.h: Albini records them in Chicago, and Touch and Go puts it out
years.p: Six days at Electrical Audio in June; Touch and Go releases it in the US, Ex Records at home. It's dedicated to Tom Cora, who died that year.
years.xp: Jack Rabid heard Albini's "best, clearest sounding, deepest production" in years. Pitchfork later put it on its Touch and Go 25 list.

years.src: The Ex: History · Wikipedia: The Ex
yt: Live at the Knitting Factory, New York, February 1999
years.h: Twenty years: Shellac at the Paradiso party, Fugazi on the road
years.p: The sold-out anniversary show has [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]] and De Kift. That year the band also plays seven shows with [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] and records In the Fishtank with [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Dizzy Spells · The Ex: History
years.h: Dizzy Spells, recorded by Albini in rural France
years.p: Cut at Black Box studio in Noyant-la-Gravoyère, out on Touch and Go in the US. A September US tour is called off after 9/11.
years.xp: Metacritic: 82; Pitchfork gave it 8.5. Some songs use texts by the poets Eduardo Galeano and Lucebert. It's bassist Luc's last studio album with the band.

years.cap: The Ex with Han Bennink, playing outdoors in Ethiopia, 2002
years.src: Pitchfork · The Guardian · The Ex: History
years.h: Free shows in Ethiopian marketplaces, with Han Bennink on drums
years.p: Half Ex songs, half Ethiopian favourites, played for free on marketplaces and theatre steps for people who'd never been to a concert.
years.xp:
Hessels had travelled there in 1996, and Ethiopian friends in Amsterdam pushed the band to go. Kids on the street asked why they'd come, Sok told Pitchfork: "But why? We already have music of our own..."

"There is no tour circuit," Hessels said. Moor: "One time we were playing in a barn on a farm and another time in the police community hall." They left their generators and amps behind for local musicians.

years.src: The Ex: History · Wikipedia: The Ex
years.h: A double bassist from the Concertgebouw Orchestra replaces Luc
years.p: Luc Klaasen left in September 2002 after 19 years; [[Rozemarie Heggen|7428a556-4fbf-40b1-b9b3-09ddb4ef3050]] makes her debut in 2003. That year the band also brings Konono Nº1 from Congo to Europe.

years.cap: The Ex at Club W71, Weikersheim, Germany, June 2004
years.src: The Ex: History · Pitchfork
yt: Building a Broken Mousetrap, Jem Cohen, 2006
years.h: Jem Cohen films them at the Knitting Factory in New York
years.p: Nine songs, shot in the city that had just hosted the Republican convention, become Building a Broken Mousetrap (2006).

years.src: Wikipedia: Turn · The Ex: History
years.h: Turn, a double album with nods to Konono and Getatchew
years.p: Albini recorded the Chicago half; the rest was done in Amsterdam. Pitchfork gave it 8.8 and said it "may be their best", 25 years in.
years.xp: It's the first record with Heggen's double bass. The Chicago Reader's Peter Margasak said she gave "the band a new focus and energy."

eras.title: Ethio-punk and show 1,371
eras.text: The band spent these years half in Amsterdam theatres and half on the road with Getatchew Mekuria, a saxophone hero of 1970s Ethiopian music. It ended with the founding singer stepping down.

years.src: The Ex: History · Wikipedia: The Ex
years.h: Twenty nights of A Clockwork Orange in a shipyard shed
years.p: The band plays the stage show with theatre group d'Electrique at the NDSM yard. Heggen leaves; Massimo Pupillo of Zu, then Colin McLean, cover bass, before Hessels and Moor take it on with baritone guitars.

years.src: The Ex: History · Pitchfork
years.h: Back in Chicago for Touch and Go's 25th birthday
years.p: The label's anniversary festival is the band's 13th trip to the US.

years.cap: The Ex live with Getatchew Mekuria
years.src: The Ex: History · Wikipedia: The Ex discography
years.h: Getatchew Mekuria, born 1935, makes a record with a punk band
years.p: Moa Anbessa comes after the 2004 Convoy tour, when the Ethiopian saxophonist was 73 and the band took him through France and Belgium.

years.cap: The Ex with dancer Melaku Belay
q: We went back to pressing up cassettes, giving them out to taxi drivers
years.src: The Ex: History · The Guardian
years.h: Ten thousand cassettes handed out to Addis Ababa taxi drivers
years.p: Celebration shows with Getatchew in Addis Ababa, on Ethiopian TV, and a tape pressing big enough to make the band known in parts of the country.

years.src: The Ex: History · Wikipedia: The Ex · Wikipedia: G.W. Sok
years.h: G.W. Sok leaves after 30 years; Arnold de Boer of Zea steps in
years.p: The band's count of Sok's performances. He wanted to put his energy into writing, graphic design and new projects; [[Arnold de Boer|e7c1b782-3130-4d5d-8fd3-69d753b78d2d]], whose band Zea the Ex had taken to Ethiopia, takes over vocals, guitar and samples.
years.xp: Sok went on to King Champion Sounds and Oiseaux-Tempête, and in 2011 published a 400-page collection of his lyrics, A Mix of Bricks & Valentines.

eras.title: No bass, no nostalgia
eras.text: With a new singer and two baritone guitars where the bass used to be, the band kept writing whole new sets instead of greatest-hits tours. Albini recorded the first album with the new lineup, and the anniversaries kept coming.

years.cap: Andy Moor with The Ex in A Coruña
years.src: Wikipedia: Catch My Shoe · The Ex: History
years.h: Catch My Shoe: De Boer's first album, and no bass player
years.p: Three days at Electrical Audio in March 2010 with Albini and [[Bob Weston|e87c3bc6-2120-4032-8137-054d0d754b8c]]; the guitarists cover the low end on baritones. Metacritic: 72.
years.xp: Critics agreed the band hadn't missed a beat, but split on the new voice: Spin found de Boer "much less bracing" than Sok, while AllMusic and Rolling Stone were warmer. One track is a cover of an Ethiopian song the band found on cassette.

years.cap: The Ex in A Coruña, November 2012
years.src: The Ex: History
years.h: Anniversary festivals in four cities mark 33⅓ years
years.p: Amsterdam, Paris, Brussels and London host the EX 33⅓ festivals, the same year as its first South America tour and Getatchew's last in Europe.

years.src: The Ex: History · The Ex: Info
years.h: Getatchew Mekuria dies
years.p: The band had played more than 100 concerts with him and had been raising money for his pension that year. Ethiopian national TV ran tributes.

years.src: The Ex: History
years.h: 27 Passports launches at an Ethiopian and Eritrean restaurant
years.p: Recorded at Electric Monkey Studio in October 2017. The same year takes them to Istanbul and to Abu Dhabi, the furthest east they'd played in 40 years.

years.src: The Ex: History
years.h: The 2,000th gig, in Leipzig
years.p: The first show of a whole new set came on March 1 in Diksmuide, Belgium, after the Covid break; the EX 45 festivals close the year.

years.src: The Ex: History · The Ex: Info
years.h: A whole set recorded in three days becomes If Your Mirror Breaks
years.p: Taped in December 2024 and mastered by Bob Weston in Chicago. The release party is at the Paradiso, with the ICP Orkest.
